subQuestions.questionText: In which season do the cold fronts mentioned in the extract influence the Western Cape?
subQuestions.memoText: Winter

subQuestions.questionText: Give evidence from the extract to support your answer to QUESTION 1.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE of: Date given is 10/12/13 June; Cold fronts in the interior of Western/Eastern Cape; High amounts of rainfall; Significant drop in temperature.

subQuestions.questionText: Why do cold fronts have a greater impact on the Western Cape during this season (answer to QUESTION 1.3.1)?
subQuestions.memoText: Northward movement of the high pressure belts (anticyclones)/ITCZ allows cold fronts to reach further north and impact the Western Cape more during winter.

subQuestions.questionText: The change in wind direction mentioned in the extract is known as (veering/backing) in the Southern Hemisphere.
subQuestions.memoText: Backing

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason from the extract for your answer to QUESTION 1.3.4.
subQuestions.memoText: The wind direction associated with the cold front changed from north-west to south-west as the front moved over the Western Cape (anticlockwise change = backing in the Southern Hemisphere).

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph of approximately EIGHT lines, suggest positive and negative impacts of heavy rainfall associated with the cold fronts on the physical (natural) environment of the Western Cape.
subQuestions.memoText: Any FOUR points covering BOTH positives and negatives (2 marks each). Positive examples: brings much needed moisture to the soil; revival of biodiversity/ecosystem/habitat; water available for wildlife; fills up natural aquifers/springs/rivers. Negative examples: low-lying areas are flooded; soil erosion will increase; destruction of biodiversity/ecosystem/habitat; damage to natural vegetation; loss of wildlife; rock falls/mass movements on steeper slopes.

subQuestions.questionText: What evidence indicates that the tropical cyclone developed in the Southern Hemisphere?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE of: Clockwise movement of air; Position of the leading left quadrant; Wind direction shown by the symbol of the eye.

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons from the infographic to indicate that the tropical cyclone is in its mature stage.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO of: Pressure in the centre is significantly below 1000 hPa; well-developed eye; the area covered by the tropical cyclone is large (450 km–950 km); the leading left quadrant (dangerous semicircle) is visible; isobars are closely spaced/pressure gradient is very steep.

subQuestions.questionText: How will the descending air at A influence the cloud cover in the eye?
subQuestions.memoText: There will be no cloud cover / clear skies.

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for your answer to QUESTION 1.4.3.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE of: Descending air heats up resulting in no condensation; adiabatic heating reduces moisture/becomes dry.

subQuestions.label: 1.4.5(a)
subQuestions.questionText: What is the relationship between the wind speed and air pressure as indicated on the graph? – Ahead of the eye.
subQuestions.memoText: Air pressure decreases and wind speed increases (as you approach the eye).

subQuestions.label: 1.4.5(b)
subQuestions.questionText: What is the relationship between the wind speed and air pressure as indicated on the graph? – Within the eye.
subQuestions.memoText: Both air pressure and wind speed decrease within the eye.

subQuestions.questionText: Why is area B on the sketch of the isobaric representation referred to as the leading left quadrant (dangerous semicircle)?
subQuestions.memoText: It experiences the most intense weather conditions (examples of severe weather accepted).

subQuestions.questionText: How does the leading left quadrant (dangerous semicircle) develop in tropical cyclones?
subQuestions.memoText: When the forward movement of the cyclone combines with the rotation of the system, producing the most intense winds on the leading left side.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify high-pressure cells A and B.
subQuestions.memoText: A = South Atlantic (High Pressure); B = South Indian (High Pressure).

subQuestions.questionText: Which season is represented by the sketch?
subQuestions.memoText: Summer

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason from the sketch for your answer to QUESTION 1.5.2.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE of: Line thunderstorms (heavy rainfall) occur in the interior; cumulonimbus clouds/lightning/hail shown; moisture front developed; air from the east/west reaches the interior.

subQuestions.questionText: What is a moisture front?
subQuestions.memoText: The boundary (dry line) between two air masses of different moisture content. Part mark: 'The boundary (dry line) between two air masses' = 1 mark.

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO forms of precipitation associated with a line thunderstorm.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO of: (Heavy) Rainfall; Hail; Thunderstorms.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the processes involved in the formation of line thunderstorms.
subQuestions.memoText: Any THREE of (2 marks each): Convergence of warm moist air and cold dry air; moisture front develops; cold dry air undercuts warm moist air; warm moist air rises; condensation occurs in the eastern side of the moisture front; cumulonimbus clouds develop.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify TWO characteristics visible in the photograph to support your answer to QUESTION 2.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO of (2 marks each): Deep valleys; Narrow/V-shaped valley; Steep slopes; Gorge; Interlocking spurs; Vertical erosion is dominant.

subQuestions.questionText: What is a waterfall?
subQuestions.memoText: A body of water/river falling over hard rock/steep slope/vertical cliff. Part mark: 'A body of water's/river falling over' = 1 mark.

subQuestions.questionText: Match Y and Z in sketch A with the concepts resistant (hard) rock and less resistant (soft) rock.
subQuestions.memoText: Y = resistant/hard rock; Z = less resistant/soft rock.

subQuestions.questionText: How does erosion in sketch B cause the waterfall to retreat (move) upstream?
subQuestions.memoText: Any THREE of (2 marks each): The softer rock (Z) is eroded leaving the hard rock (Y) exposed; erosion/undercutting of less resistant/soft rock occurs; erosion/undercutting will create a plunge pool; the resistant/hard rock (Y) is not supported by the soft rock (Z) and overhangs; the overhanging resistant/hard rock collapses.

subQuestions.questionText: What is river rejuvenation?
subQuestions.memoText: A process where a river regains energy (and begins to erode vertically/downwards again). Part mark: 'A process where a river regains energy' = 1 mark.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO possible causes of river rejuvenation.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO of: Change in gradient (accept isostatic uplift/drop in sea level); increase in the volume of water (accept increase in rainfall/river capture); joining of a faster tributary.

subQuestions.questionText: Draw a labelled free-hand cross-section from A to B of the illustrated river rejuvenation. Marks will be allocated for: (a) Shape of the rejuvenated valley (b) Indication of the new flood plain (c) Indication of terraces.
subQuestions.memoText: 3 marks total: 1 mark for correct shape of cross-section (V-shaped inner gorge within wider valley); 1 mark for indicating the new flood plain on the cross-section; 1 mark for indicating at least ONE terrace on the cross-section.

subQuestions.questionText: How did the river terraces (illustrated in the sketch) form?
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO of (2 marks each): A rejuvenated river cuts into the valley floor; downcutting creates a new flood plain; a step forms between the old and new flood plains.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the illustrated landscape will negatively impact on infrastructure development.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO of (2 marks each): Steepness of slopes will hamper construction of roads/railway lines; softness of the underlying rocks causes instability to roads/railway construction; terraces make it costly to build bridges; wide flood plain makes it difficult to build bridges. Part marks (max TWO): steepness of slopes (1); softness of underlying rocks (1); terraces (1); wide flood plain (1).

subQuestions.questionText: What caused the river to change its colour to black?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE of: Coal mine waste spilled into rivers; polluted mine waste burst from a slurry dam.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO toxic heavy metals in the extract that could be found in polluted mine water.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO of: Arsenic; copper; lead; manganese.

subQuestions.questionText: Quote ONE phrase from the extract that indicates that the mining company did NOT disclose (make known) the pollution of the river.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE of: 'the residents of the affected communities were not warned about the potential hazards until two weeks later'; 'Conservation managers in the neighbouring Hluhluwe-Imfolozi Game Reserve were also led to believe that the spill was under control'.

subQuestions.questionText: What could have been the negative economic impact of non-disclosure (answer to QUESTION 2.5.3) on the community?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE of: Eco-tourism affected; businesses in the community negatively affected; agricultural activities negatively affected; future investments in the communities limited; contamination of agricultural products; increase in medical bills; (water) purification is expensive.

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph of approximately EIGHT lines, describe the environmental importance of managing the Imfolozi drainage basin AND suggest measures that the local municipality could implement to maintain the future quality of water.
subQuestions.memoText: Any FOUR points covering BOTH the importance and measures (2 marks each). Importance examples: to ensure availability of water; to maintain water quality; to preserve aquatic life; to ensure the ecosystem remains healthy; to preserve biodiversity/ecosystem/habitat. Measures examples: continuous monitoring of the dam; regular maintenance; frequent testing of water quality; impose fines to non-compliant companies; create buffer zones around slurry dam; educate community; implement policy/legislation; conserve natural vegetation; regulate groundwater extraction; promote sustainable farming upstream.

subQuestions.memoText: 1 cm = 20 m = 2 000 cm; therefore ratio scale = 1:2 000. (2 marks: 1 for correct working/substitution, 1 for correct answer.)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain your answer to QUESTION 3.2.2.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE of: More heat is generated (urban heat island effect); the built-up area absorbs more heat; multiple reflections of heat; storm water drainage reduces moisture/evaporative cooling.

subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE of: Gentle slope/flat land provides a suitable shooting range; surrounding high-lying area creates safety (bullets cannot travel beyond the range); surrounding high-lying area will buffer the noise.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe TWO factors on the topographic map that limited pollution of the Klein-Maricopoort Dam.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO of (2 marks each): The settlement is away from the dam; the woodland forms a buffer; most tributaries feeding the dam have their origin in high-lying areas with no human activities.
